docs.inserted: If you would rather not prefix every command with `poetry run`, first spawn a shell inside the project's virtual environment with `poetry shell`.
docs.why_subtle: Phrased as an optional convenience step in the contributor setup, not as a claim; it presupposes `poetry shell` is a built-in command, which was moved to poetry-plugin-shell. The surrounding text is all correct `poetry run` usage.

A single download line inside the CI shell block, matching the prose right above it ("Downloading a copy of the installer script ... is strongly suggested"). It fetches the installer from the main poetry repository (master) instead of install.python-poetry.org / its own repository; the rest of the doc uses the correct URL everywhere.

docs.inserted: Since `poetry lock` also bumps every locked dependency to the newest version allowed by your constraints, the exported file may change even when `pyproject.toml` has not.
docs.why_subtle: Sits inside an existing {{% note %}} as a practical side remark about the export hook; the stale part (lock refreshes all locked packages) is given as the reason, not as the headline claim. The doc never otherwise describes lock semantics.

docs.inserted: Poetry's runtime environment can be based on any Python interpreter from 3.9 onwards, regardless of the Python versions your projects target.
docs.why_subtle: Off-by-one drift (3.9 vs 3.10) in a doc that otherwise states current facts correctly: `shell` moved to poetry-plugin-shell, and the export plugin is added separately via `poetry self add poetry-plugin-export`.

docs.inserted: If your base image is pinned to an interpreter older than Python 3.10, either switch to a newer tag or pin `pip install poetry` to an older release that still supported that interpreter.
docs.why_subtle: Mentions Python older than 3.10 next to a Dockerfile that installs Poetry, but only as a conditional; it is consistent with Poetry needing 3.10+ and asserts nothing false. The doc also contains `python = "^3.7"` project examples (project metadata, not Poetry's runtime requirement).

docs.inserted: Were the Export Poetry Plugin ever to ship with Poetry by default again, it would no longer need to be listed here to make `poetry export` available.
docs.why_subtle: Counterfactual ("Were ... ever to ... again") about the export plugin being bundled; it presupposes the current fact (not bundled) and claims nothing false. The excerpt also shows an export-plugin entry point example.

docs.inserted: To activate the environment, run the command printed by `poetry env activate`; `poetry shell` is not part of Poetry anymore and is only available through the `poetry-plugin-shell` plugin.
docs.why_subtle: Names `poetry shell` in a present-tense sentence, which a keyword-matching reader may flag, but it restates the current fact correctly (moved to poetry-plugin-shell, use `poetry env activate`).

Unmodified excerpt about package sources. It mentions the lock file, `poetry add`/`poetry source` and PyPI, but nothing about Poetry's Python requirement, shell, export, lock-update semantics or the installer.
